attachments.attachment_title: Report - Addendum to the Brian Coburn and Cumberland Transitway EA Study - REV.pdf

sub_agendas_items.description: File No. ACS2025-PDB-TP-0020 - Orléans West-Innes (2), Beacon Hill-Cyrville (11), Orléans South-Navan (19)
sub_agendas_items.minutes: A technical amendment motion was moved by Councillor L. Dudas to include comments that were inadvertently omitted from the report. The motion was CARRIED by the Committee and the item was CARRIED AS AMENDED.

motions.motion_text:
Report Recommendation(s)
That the Public Works and Infrastructure Committee approve the Statement of Work to update the Brian Coburn Boulevard Extension and Cumberland Transitway (Blair Road to Navan Road) Environmental Assessment Study, as outlined in this report.

WHEREAS the Ward Councillor’s comments were inadvertently omitted from the report on this item;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the “Comments by the Ward Councillor” section of the report be amended to include the following text:
Comments from Councillor Laura Dudas (Ward 2):
For far too long, Orléans has been held back by a lack of direct transportation connections to the central and southern parts of our city. While our community has grown rapidly, the infrastructure has not kept pace. Development has overburdened the few east-west corridors available, leaving residents feeling frustrated and disconnected.
This is an issue I’ve been advocating for since before my time as Councillor, which speaks to how deeply it matters to our community. Both the Cumberland Transitway and the Brian Coburn Extension are critical links that would finally connect Orléans to the broader city. These projects are not just about roads and transit; they are about equity, access, and opportunity. They would provide vital connections for motorists, cyclists, and transit users alike.
As we move forward, it is essential that all future design proposals continue to undergo thorough and meaningful community consultation. We must ensure that the communities impacted by these projects are actively involved in the planning process, and that future transportation infrastructure reflects our needs today while preparing us for the growth and challenges of tomorrow.

sub_agendas_items.title: All-Way Stop at Solarium Avenue and Andromeda Road

motions.motion_text: That theRules of Procedurebe suspended to consider the following motion due to road safety concerns in a residential neighbourhood with increased speeding incidents and to allow this item to rise to the Council meeting of November 12, 2025;

WHEREAS there is currently a temporary all-way stop control installed at the intersection of Solarium Avenue and Andromeda Road in the Riverside South community; and
WHEREAS this intersection is located immediately adjacent to St. Gianna School, where a significant number of students and families cross daily during morning arrival and afternoon dismissal periods; and
WHEREAS there is a temporary sign on Solarium Avenue stating, “Cross traffic does not stop after October 31,” indicating that the existing all-way stop is intended to be removed following that date; and
WHEREAS members of the community, including parents, residents, and school representatives, have expressed ongoing concerns regarding pedestrian and traf-fic safety at this intersection; and
WHEREAS the temporary stop signs have proven effective in improving safety and reducing vehicle speeds in the area, thereby addressing community concerns; and
WHEREAS the local community has expressed strong support for maintaining the stop signs on a permanent basis to ensure continued pedestrian safety and promote a safe environment for all road users;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the existing temporary all-way stop control at the intersection of Solarium Avenue and Andromeda Road be retained.

sub_agendas_items.title: Vision Zero Initiatives for City’s Heavy Equipment Fleet
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by Councillor L. Johnson
On October 16, 2025, a commercial dump truck struck and killed a five year old boy in Ottawa’s Overbrook neighbourhood. To avoid such tragic deaths, Other munici-palities such as Toronto are leveraging Vision Zero design principles across mul-tiple City departments, such as Fleet.
Can Fleet Services outline by the end of Q1 2026 any heavy vehicle safety im-provements or initiatives the City may consider for its heavy equipment fleet which align with the “vision zero” strategies being implemented by other municipalities, such as Toronto.
